realm_scorer_handoff.proposal_summary: Collect both airport guests in one trip using Pat's car, on mapped routes that the disruptions do not touch, and finish it well before 14:00. Pat arrives at W (Wedding venue) at 12:00 with a 5-seat car. Pat drives W→B (40 min) and gets to B (Boston Airport) about 12:40, after Jamie lands at 12:30. Pat picks up Alex (landed 11:00) and Jamie, then drives B→T (30 min) to reach T (Tailor shop) about 13:10, before it closes at 14:00. Pat then drives T→W (15 min) and arrives about 13:25 plus time spent at the tailor. That leaves more than 90 minutes before photo_time 15:00. This avoids the hotel-church closure (13:00 for 39 min) and the airport-hotel delay (+17 min from 14:00). It also avoids the short-sighted option of sending a vehicle for Alex at 11:00, which would need a second airport trip near or after 14:00, when the delay starts. The fleet vehicles (van, car1, car2) stay as backups because their start points are not in the travel-time table. Any use of them must allow for the closure and treat the 17-min delay as continuing.

Keep the single combined airport trip from episode 1, with two changes. First, add travel time for the jitter on every leg. Second, set a fixed limit on time at the tailor, so the photo_time margin is a stated number rather than a loose claim. Pat starts at W (Wedding venue) at 12:00 in a 5-seat car. Pat drives W→B, which is 40 min nominal or about 41 min with jitter (×1.020687), reaching B (Boston Airport) at about 12:41. That is after Jamie lands at 12:30. Pat picks up Alex (landed 11:00) and Jamie, using 3 of 5 seats. Pat drives B→T, 30 min nominal or about 31 min with jitter, reaching T (Tailor shop) at about 13:12. The tailor stop is capped so that Pat leaves T by 13:59 at the latest, before tailor_closes at 14:00. Pat then drives T→W, 15 min nominal or about 16 min with jitter, reaching W by about 14:15 in the worst case. That is at least 45 min before photo_time at 15:00 and well before wedding_deadline at 18:00. This plan avoids myopic choices: there is no separate early trip for Alex that would force a second airport run into the 14:00 delay. It also does not underestimate route times: jitter is added to every mapped leg, and the airport-hotel delay of +17 min from 14:00 is treated as continuing. The hotel-church closure (13:00, 39 min) is treated as still in place after 13:39 until the road is actually seen to reopen. The fleet vehicles (van, car1, car2) stay as backups only, because their start points are not in the travel-time table.

Doing that would undercut the episode 2 observation (×1.020687), which is exactly the stale-world error this sequence tests. So each leg uses the larger of the nominal time and the worst observed jitter, rounded up: W→B 41 min, B→T 31 min, T→W 16 min, B→W 41 min.
